title: Who did it? Impersonal and passive style
title_target: Det står aldrig vem som gör något.
goal: Read Swedish officialese and news Swedish — where nobody seems to do anything — and turn it back into plain, human Swedish.
bekal: the s-passive in every tense, including *det har framförts* and *beräknas påbörjas*
four ways of not saying who: *man*, *en*, *det sägs*, *enligt*
wave: Go back to Unit 4: reread the hedging verbs (*verkar*, *tycks*, *sägs*, *lär*) and make five sentences about your own city that start with *Det sägs att…* — you will meet *sägs* again in this unit, now as part of a whole passive system.

dialogs.title: Text — Samråd om Ringvägen
dialogs.intro: Dian is collecting material for her thesis on sustainable cities. In her mailbox she finds a consultation letter from the City of Stockholm about rebuilding a big street on Södermalm. It is a perfect specimen of official Swedish, so she reads it line by line.

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Stockholms stad planerar att bygga om Ringvägen mellan Götgatan och Hornsgatan.
lines.id: The City of Stockholm is planning to rebuild Ringvägen between Götgatan and Hornsgatan.
lines.literal: Stockholm's city plans to build over Ring-road-the between …

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Arbetet beräknas påbörjas under våren 2027 och väntas pågå i cirka arton månader.
lines.id: Work is estimated to start in the spring of 2027 and is expected to last about eighteen months.
lines.literal: work-the is-calculated be-begun during spring-the 2027 and is-expected go-on in about eighteen months

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Under byggtiden kommer framkomligheten att begränsas.
lines.id: During construction, access will be restricted.
lines.literal: during building-time-the comes passability-the to be-limited

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Vissa busshållplatser flyttas tillfälligt.
lines.id: Some bus stops will be moved temporarily.
lines.literal: certain bus-stops are-moved temporarily

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Det har framförts önskemål om bredare cykelbanor och fler träd längs gatan.
lines.id: Requests have been made for wider bike lanes and more trees along the street.
lines.literal: it has been-put-forward wishes about broader bike-lanes and more trees along street-the

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Förslaget har tagits fram i samråd med boende och verksamheter i området.
lines.id: The proposal has been drawn up in consultation with residents and businesses in the area.
lines.literal: proposal-the has been-taken forth in consultation with living-ones and businesses in area-the

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Synpunkter på förslaget lämnas skriftligen senast den 15 mars.
lines.id: Comments on the proposal must be submitted in writing by March 15.
lines.literal: viewpoints on proposal-the are-left in-writing latest the 15 March

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Inkomna synpunkter kommer att sammanställas och beaktas i det fortsatta arbetet.
lines.id: All comments received will be compiled and taken into account as the work continues.
lines.literal: in-come viewpoints come to be-compiled and be-considered in the continued work-the

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Handlingarna kan läsas på stadens webbplats eller hämtas på stadsdelsförvaltningen.
lines.id: The documents can be read on the city's website or picked up at the district administration office.
lines.literal: documents-the can be-read on city-the's website or be-fetched at district-administration-the

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Enligt trafiknämndens beslut ska ombyggnaden vara klar senast hösten 2029.
lines.id: According to the traffic committee's decision, the rebuilding is to be finished by the fall of 2029 at the latest.
lines.literal: according-to traffic-committee-the's decision shall rebuilding-the be ready latest autumn-the 2029

lines.speaker: Text:
lines.text: Frågor besvaras av projektledaren vardagar kl. 9–12.
lines.id: Questions are answered by the project manager on weekdays from 9 to 12.
lines.literal: questions are-answered by project-leader-the weekdays o'clock 9–12

notes: **Beräknas påbörjas** — two passives in a row: "is estimated to be started". Verbs like *beräknas* (is estimated), *väntas* (is expected), *anses* (is considered) and *sägs* (is said) take a bare infinitive, exactly like English "is said **to** be" — but without any *att*. *Han anses vara landets bäste kock.*

**Kommer framkomligheten att begränsas** — the passive infinitive is simply the infinitive + *-s*: *begränsa* → *begränsas*. That is why the future passive looks like this: *kommer att begränsas*, *ska byggas*, *måste lämnas*. **Framkomlighet** (literally "get-through-ability") is a typical official noun; a normal person would say *det blir svårt att ta sig fram*.

**Det har framförts önskemål** — Swedish happily puts an empty *det* in the subject slot and the real subject later. Literally "there have been put forward wishes". The supine passive ends in **-ts** or **-ats**: *framförts*, *tagits*, *byggts*, *beaktats*. Say it **deh hahr FRAHM-föts ÖN-skeh-mohl** — *rt* melts.

**Lämnas skriftligen** — the present passive here is not a description but an **instruction**: "are (to be) submitted" = "must be submitted". Signs and forms are full of these: *Dörren hålls stängd*, *Avgiften betalas i förskott*. **Senast** means "at the latest, no later than" — *senast den 15 mars* = "by March 15".

**Inkomna synpunkter** — *inkommen* ("come in") is a past participle used as an adjective, a hallmark of written officialese. You will meet many more of these in Unit 7. **Samt** is a formal *och*; you will see it in letters and contracts but rarely hear it in a kitchen.
**Enligt** (according to) names a source without making it the grammatical subject — the classic newspaper and authority move. Pronounce it **EHN-lit**: the *g* is silent in normal speech.

grammars.title: The s-passive in all its forms
body: You met the s-passive in Svenska 102. At B2 the challenge is not forming it but recognizing it in every tense, because official texts use almost nothing else. The rule is simple: take the active form and add **-s**. Present tense *-er* drops the *-er* first (*läser* → *läses*), and the supine becomes **-ts / -ats / -its**.
after: The agent, if mentioned at all, comes with **av**: *Frågor besvaras **av** projektledaren* (Questions are answered **by** the project manager). In officialese the agent is usually left out — which is the whole point.

With **det** as an empty subject you get the impersonal passive, which English can only imitate with "there": *Det har framförts kritik* (Criticism has been voiced), *Det dansades hela natten* (There was dancing all night).

grammars.title: Passive verbs that report: anses, sägs, väntas, beräknas
body: A small group of passive verbs is the backbone of cautious, impersonal reporting. They are followed by a bare infinitive — no *att* — and they keep the speaker at a safe distance from the claim.

head: Verb
English
Example
rows: Hon **anses** vara en av de bästa forskarna.

after: Notice the perfect infinitive in the last row: *ha skadats* (to have been injured). Unit 12 returns to *uppges* and its media cousins.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Klarspråk på biblioteket
dialogs.intro: Dian takes the letter to the library where Elin works. Elin has spent years helping people decode letters from the authorities, and she has opinions.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Elin, har du en minut? Jag fattar ingenting av det här brevet från staden.
lines.id: Elin, do you have a minute? I don't get anything in this letter from the city.
lines.literal: Elin, have you a minute? I grasp nothing of this here letter-the from city-the

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Visa. Aha, typiskt myndighetsspråk. ”Arbetet beräknas påbörjas” — vem beräknar, liksom?
lines.id: Show me. Aha, typical bureaucratese. "Work is estimated to start" — who's doing the estimating, you know?
lines.literal: show. aha, typical authority-language … who calculates, like?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Precis. Det står aldrig vem som gör något. Allt bara flyttas och beaktas.
lines.id: Exactly. It never says who's doing anything. Everything just gets moved and taken into account.
lines.literal: exactly. it stands never who that does something. everything just is-moved and is-considered

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Det är s-passivet. Det låter sakligt, men det döljer vem som har ansvaret.
lines.id: That's the s-passive. It sounds objective, but it hides who's responsible.
lines.literal: it is s-passive-the. it sounds factual, but it hides who that has responsibility-the

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och ”det har framförts önskemål” — vilka har framfört dem?
lines.id: And "requests have been made" — who made them?
lines.literal: and … which-ones have put-forward them?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Det får man aldrig veta. Det sägs att de boende vill ha fler träd, men ingen står för det.
lines.id: You never find out. Supposedly the residents want more trees, but nobody puts their name to it.
lines.literal: that gets one never know. it is-said that the living-ones want have more trees, but nobody stands for it

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hur skulle man skriva det på klarspråk, då?
lines.id: So how would you write it in plain language?
lines.literal: how should one write it on clear-language, then?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: ”Vi börjar bygga våren 2027. Vi räknar med att det tar ungefär ett och ett halvt år.”
lines.id: "We'll start building in the spring of 2027. We expect it to take about a year and a half."
lines.literal: we begin build spring-the 2027. we count with that it takes about one and one half year

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Mycket bättre! Men får en myndighet verkligen skriva ”vi”?
lines.id: Much better! But is a government agency really allowed to write "we"?
lines.literal: much better! but may an authority really write "we"?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Absolut. Enligt språklagen ska språket i offentlig verksamhet vara vårdat, enkelt och begripligt.
lines.id: Absolutely. According to the Language Act, the language of the public sector must be careful, simple and comprehensible.
lines.literal: absolutely. according-to language-law-the shall language-the in public activity be cared-for, simple and comprehensible

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det citerar jag i uppsatsen. En känner sig ju dum när en inte förstår ett brev om sin egen gata.
lines.id: I'm quoting that in my thesis. You feel stupid when you can't understand a letter about your own street.
lines.literal: that quote I in essay-the. one feels self ju stupid when one not understands a letter about one's own street

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: ”En känner sig” — du har lyssnat på poddar, märker jag.
lines.id: "One feels" — you've been listening to podcasts, I can tell.
lines.literal: one feels self — you have listened on pods, notice I

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, det sägs att ”en” är mer könsneutralt än ”man”. Fast mina lärare skriver fortfarande ”man”.
lines.id: Yes, they say "en" is more gender-neutral than "man". Though my teachers still write "man".
lines.literal: yes, it is-said that "one" is more gender-neutral than "man". though my teachers write still "man"

notes: **Jag fattar ingenting** — *fatta* is the everyday word for "understand, get" (*Fattar du?* "Get it?"). In writing, *fatta* means "to take" in fixed phrases: *fatta ett beslut* (make a decision), *fatta mod* (take courage). Officialese loves *beslut har fattats*.

**Vem som gör något** — in an indirect question, when the question word is the **subject**, Swedish inserts *som*: *vem **som** har ansvaret*, *vad **som** hände*. Without *som* the sentence sounds broken to Swedish ears.

**Det får man aldrig veta** — *man* is the default impersonal subject ("you, one, people"). Its object form is *en* and its possessive is *ens*: *Det gör **en** trött*, *när **ens** egen familj inte förstår*. But the reflexive possessive is still *sin*: *Man ska ta hand om **sin** hälsa*.

**En känner sig ju dum** — using *en* as a subject instead of *man* is old in northern dialects and has spread as a gender-neutral alternative, because *man* is spelled like the word for "a man". You will hear it in podcasts and read it in some newspapers; in most formal writing *man* is still the norm. Recognize both, and choose *man* when unsure.
**Står för det** — *stå för något* means "to stand behind, to vouch for something": *Jag står för vad jag sa.* It is exactly what the passive avoids.

**Språklagen** (2009) really does say that public-sector language must be *vårdat, enkelt och begripligt*. That sentence is the legal basis of the Swedish *klarspråk* movement — the plain-language work coordinated by Språkrådet.

grammars.title: Four ways not to say who
body: Swedish has a whole toolbox for statements without a clear person behind them. They are not interchangeable: each one creates a different distance between the speaker and the claim.

head: Tool
Effect
Example
English
rows: That kind of thing makes you tired.
rumor, hearsay — you keep your distance
Det sägs att hon ska flytta.
you name the source but not yourself
Enligt polisen var det en olycka.
According to the police, it was an accident.
the action matters, the actor doesn't
The school is closing on Friday.

after: In speech, Swedes overwhelmingly choose *man*. In news, *enligt* and the s-passive dominate. In official letters, the s-passive is so frequent that plain-language guides list it as the number one thing to cut.

blocks.text: Swedish authorities have been told for decades — first by government guidelines, since 2009 by law — to write plainly. Old habits survive, though, and you will still receive letters from Skatteverket, landlords and universities full of the phrases on the left. Learn to recognize them; avoid them in your own writing unless you are imitating a form.

head: Officialese
Plain Swedish
English
rows: Anna Berg tar hand om ditt ärende.
Anna Berg is handling your case.
Skicka med de papper som behövs.
You pay the fee in advance.

blocks.title: The klarspråk checklist
items: Write **vi** for the authority and **du** for the reader.
Use active verbs with a real subject: *Vi beslutade*, not *Beslut fattades*.
Put the most important information first — what the reader must do, and by when.
Prefer short everyday verbs: *få* (not *erhålla*), *börja* (not *påbörja*), *ge* (not *tillhandahålla*), *gälla* (not *avse*).
One idea per sentence; around fifteen to twenty words is plenty.

blocks.text: Newspaper headlines compress the passive even further. Often the auxiliary disappears and only a participle is left — the Swedish equivalent of English "Man arrested after robbery".

head: Headline
Full sentence
English
rows: Man gripen efter rån i Malmö
En man har gripits efter ett rån i Malmö.
Man arrested after robbery in Malmö
En ny bro har invigts i Umeå.
Tåg ställs in i hela landet
Tåg ställs in i hela landet.
Proposal expected to be passed today

blocks.text: *Klubba* comes from the chairperson's gavel (*klubba*) striking the table when a decision is made — a nice example of how Swedish meeting culture leaks into the news.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Svenska 102, Unit 5
items: There you met the s-passive on signs: *Kaffet serveras kl 8*, *Huset byggdes 1890*.
Now add the supine: *Huset har byggts om två gånger*, *Kaffet har serverats*.
And the modal passive: *Huset måste byggas om*, *Kaffet kan beställas i kassan*.

answers: byggs — togs — framförts — besvaras — byggdes — beaktas
